description: This plot illustrates the relationship between layer number and both max activation value and first token attention score for different attention configurations. The x-axis is labeled “Layer” and has a linear scale ranging from 0 to 20, with tick labels at integer values. The y-axis is split into two panels; the left panel is labeled “Max Activation Value” with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 400 and units of unspecified value, with tick labels at integer multiples of 100. The right panel is labeled “First token attention score” with a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick labels at intervals of 0.2.  There are three lines displayed on the plot. The first line, representing “attn_output”, is solid, red, and begins at approximately 10 at layer 0, rises to a peak of approximately 350 at layer 6, then declines to approximately 10 at layer 20. The second line, representing “attn_residual”, is dashed, green, and begins at approximately 10 at layer 0, rises to a peak of approximately 300 at layer 6, then declines to approximately 20 at layer 20. The third line, representing “fm_residual”, is dash-dotted, blue, and begins at approximately 10 at layer 0, rises to a peak of approximately 250 at layer 6, then declines to approximately 10 at layer 20.  For the first token attention score panel, the “attn_output” line is solid, red, and begins at approximately 0.95 at layer 0, declines to approximately 0.05 at layer 6, and remains relatively stable at approximately 0.02 to 0.04 for the remainder of the x-axis. The “attn_residual” line is dashed, green, and begins at approximately 0.95 at layer 0, declines to approximately 0.1 at layer 6, and remains relatively stable at approximately 0.02 to 0.05 for the remainder of the x-axis. The “fm_residual” line is dash-dotted, blue, and begins at approximately 0.95 at layer 0, declines to approximately 0.1 at layer 6, and remains relatively stable at approximately 0.02 to 0.05 for the remainder of the x-axis.
